newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police chief said only half-sure on attacker.
newsitem.headline: Japan police chief said only half-sure on attacker.

text.p: Japan's top policeman, shot last year at the start of a probe into the cult accused of the Tokyo subway attack, said he is only half-sure a policeman official say confessed to the shooting did it, news reports said on Tuesday.

"My impression of the confessions is that there is a 50-percent chance they are true," National Police Agency (NPA) Director-General Takaji Kunimatsu was quoted as saying by the Asahi Shimbun newspaper.

Government officials said last week that a junior police officer who belonged to the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) was being questioned after confessing to the near-fatal shooting of Kunimatsu in March last year.
"I felt myself go weak when I heard the report (of the policeman's confession)," Kunimatsu said.
The Mainichi Shimbun quoted him as saying that he learned of the confession in mid-October, nearly six months after it was made.
The delay in reporting the confession by the local police to the NPA, the higher authority, has led to media charges that the local police covered it up to avoid embarrassment.
A senior police officer in charge of the investigation was replaced on Tuesday.
The confession came to light only after Japanese media followed up an anonymous letter accusing local police of a cover-up in not passing on the confession to higher authorities.

According to media reports, the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department did not pass on the confession to the NPA because the man had given conflicting testimonies and still appeared to be under the sway of the cult.
Kunimatsu said the confession and investigation in general had not been well handled.
"The handling of the case jeopardised the public trust (in the police force)," the Mainichi quoted him as saying.

Officials said that in his confession, the officer said he acted on the orders of cult members in order to disrupt police investigations into the Tokyo subway gas attack on March 20, 1995, which killed 12 people and harmed 6,000 others.
Senior cult members named by the officer have denied the allegations.
Sect guru Shoko Asahara and about 100 of his cult followers are currently on trial for the gas attack and other crimes.
